features.note: The 2 ear mounting holes now READ as dark bores on the flange surface (were seated INSIDE the flange = invisible). A dark disc acting as a bore only works if it is the surface the eye lands on.
Bays render as recessed framed openings with handles and green LEDs. No regression.

TWO un-burials fixed here: the RJ45 SHIELD was a solid plate that buried its own throat (the jack read as a metallic RECTANGLE — exactly the failure the critical names, 'a dark cavity with a visible keyway, not a printed rectangle'), and the NMC PLATE was a solid plate 0.2 mm in front of the whole assembly. Now the RJ45 reads as a DARK CAVITY inside its metallic cage (verified in an orchestrator crop). Same buried-front defect, one level down at 16 mm instead of 445.

important_features.note: No regression; lamps still per-channel green-dominant/blue-dominant.

defects: Chassis colour + front layout remain declared inferences (open items).

mechanical.notes: 12/12 suites. Console clean; offline clean (orchestrator-verified). Budget 82/200 draws (41%), 2176/350000 tris (0.6%), 19 unique geometries cache-covered. THE INSTRUMENT THIS PASS ADDS TO THE LADDER: 'drawn but never seen' — for every visible mesh, cast rays from the ACTUALLY-resolved camera positions of each declared capture state and ask whether any observer-facing part of its surface is reachable; a mesh no declared state can see is cost without benefit and, far more often, an ERROR not an optimization opportunity. It only became possible once the front opened in lighting-camera, and had it existed three passes earlier it would have reported the whole buried front immediately — the argument for it being part of the pass. It found THREE MORE burials, same family: (1) the RJ45 shield (solid plate) buried its own throat, (2) the NMC plate (solid, 0.2 mm proud) buried the jack, (3) the ear holes seated inside the flange. Fixed via a frameBars() helper extracted because three hand-built frames in one file is the signal for one — without CSG a hole must be ASSEMBLED, and assembling by hand three times is three chances to build a solid plate; the helper makes the correct construction the easy one and the drawn-but-never-seen check catches the rest. Verified: 0 of 82 visible meshes unreachable, 0 front pieces hidden; 0 duplicate material signatures (full-signature compare); no instancing (12 reps at 41% budget would cost the named meshes every containment/completeness/visibility guard addresses BY NAME); no texture resize (measured in surface). Also fixed two checks that miscounted after the refactor (traceability counted the 4 frame bars as 4 RJ45 on a chassis the evidence says has one — count the assembly, not the meshes).

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. This optimization pass did DEFECT-FINDING, not just budget-trimming: the new 'drawn but never seen' visibility instrument — which only became possible once the front was un-buried, and which would have caught the buried front three passes earlier — found three more burials of the same class (RJ45 throat, NMC jack, ear holes), each a solid plate where an opening belonged. The frameBars() helper eliminates the class rather than the cases, and the visibility check backstops what escapes. The RJ45 now reads as the dark cavity its critical requires (verified in a crop), the ear bores read on the flange, no instancing (named meshes protected), offline clean, no regression. Cleared to P6 — after which the FMPS asset is COMPLETE.
